Cross-host determinism does not hold.

CI (ubuntu-24.04/x86-64) built 2ef4fdad0bef5c9b0bb88c1c5c651fb3b905be0f00364b4e36adda0fdeb33a2c;
the macOS/arm64 host built e08db880837bb0d2a90e7d23528aeefc116423f3240e8fd09dac0ae45313cac6.
Same source, same pin, same SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, same volume ID, same pinned Rust
channel. Both hosts are internally stable — two builds byte-identical on each.

So profile.toml's `deterministic_rebuilds = 2` is a same-host claim, and the
build is host-deterministic rather than reproducible. Checking the claim from
outside instead of reading `reproducible_pair_checked` back off the receipt is
what surfaced this; the receipt is true and says less than a reader assumes.

Recorded in docs/reproduction.md; architecture.md and roadmap.md corrected.
Narrowing it is not part of this pass.

Determinism gap diagnosed. The two BOOTX64.EFI binaries are the same size with identical section tables and public symbols; 31.3% of bytes differ, 33.4% of .text. Same instruction stream, different call targets, so functions are laid out in a different order.

Not paths and not compiler version: only the LLD PDB name hash differs between the two binaries, and both hosts run rustc 1.95.0 with LLVM 22.1.2. --remap-path-prefix would not help. The remaining candidate is the host toolchain build, which points at a digest-pinned container.

This confirms the diagnosis: the divergence was the host build of the toolchain. The container digest differs from both host-native digests, as expected, since the container rustc is a third build of 1.95.0 and is the one now pinned. make image remains host-deterministic; only make image-container carries the cross-host property.

Two builds on one host are byte-identical, and this was the atom that found the limit: the two hosts disagreed while both were green. Diagnosed to function layout in .text, ruled out paths and compiler version, and fixed by pinning the toolchain. Three container builds across two architectures now agree on e46c4060.
